units.text: I woke up in the dark, and something was breathing right over my bed.
I looked up, and two black holes stared back at me.
Where its eyes should be, there was only empty darkness, and it was leaking something black.
A blue mask.
A black hoodie.
No nose, and no mouth.
And this was not the first time it had come for me.
So what did it want?
And where was my brother?
Let us go back to the beginning.
My name is Mitch.
The bank took my family's house, so I moved in with my brother, Edwin.
We had not seen each other for ten years, so we were both happy.
For one whole week, everything was normal.
I unpacked, and I slept, and I got used to the quiet house.
Then, one night at about one in the morning, I heard rustling outside.
I thought it was a raccoon, so I ignored it.
The next morning, I told Edwin about it, and he agreed.
The next night, I heard my window open.
Then came a loud thump, as if something had climbed inside.
I sat up fast and looked around my room.
There was nothing there.
In the morning, Edwin dropped his coffee cup the moment he saw me.
He held up a mirror, and I saw a deep cut across my cheek.
At the hospital, the doctor said I must have been sleepwalking.
Then he showed me something that made my blood run cold.
There was a neat, stitched line on my side.
"You somehow lost your left kidney last night. We do not know how, Mitch. I am sorry."
The next night was my breaking point.
Around midnight, I woke up, and I froze.
A creature was staring down at me, face to face.
It wore a black hoodie and a dark blue mask, with no nose and no mouth.
But the worst part was its eyes.
It had none.
There were only empty black sockets, with a black liquid dripping out.
I grabbed the camera from the mantel and took a picture.
The moment I did, it lunged at me, and reached for my chest with its claws.
I kicked it in the face as hard as I could.
Then I grabbed my wallet, because I knew I would need money, and I ran out into the night.
I ran until I reached the woods near Edwin's house.
Then I tripped on a rock, and everything went black.
I woke up in the hospital, and the same doctor came in.
"I have good news and bad news, Mitch. The good news is that your injuries are small, and your parents are coming to take you home."
I sighed with relief.
"The bad news is that your brother has been killed by something. I am sorry."
My parents drove me back to Edwin's house, to collect my things.
I was scared, but I stayed calm.
I went into my room and took my camera.
Then I stopped dead in the hallway.
I saw my brother there, and I could not look for long.
Next to him lay something small.
I picked it up, and I walked to my parents' car without a word.
Inside the car, I looked at what I was holding, and I nearly threw up.
It was the part of me that the creature had stolen, black with that same dark liquid.
This story is inspired by the Eyeless Jack creepypasta, first posted by a user named Azelf5000, in twenty twelve.
Would you have stayed in that house a second night?
